verified.summary:
Scope checked and fine. In /home/alex/VistaColosseum/.worktrees/br-2026-10-04-p0-queue, phase-5 resolves to 87271f1 (also HEAD) and phase-4 to 96abf7f. The three-dot diff lists 46 files. The app/ part is maker_suggestion.dart (new), home_screen.dart, home_screen_test.dart and order_ticket_test.dart. The only uncommitted change is baton-runner/.../log.md.

All six findings hold when checked against the tree. Five are gaps in the tests and one is a small contrast miss on the advisory badge. None is a product bug, none is permanent, and none is CRITICAL or HIGH. I merged the reference-line finding with the tautological referencePrice finding, because a single rendered-text check fixes both.

One reviewer's "verified as correct" claim is wrong: tautology-hunt says the app does not clamp text scale. app/lib/main.dart clamps it to 1.3 (MediaQuery.withClampedTextScaling, maxScaleFactor 1.3). Their conclusion that the 1.3x overflow test is real still holds, because 1.3 is the clamp ceiling.

Nothing must be fixed before merge. All survivors can be fixed after.

findings.title: Ticket-prefill test cannot tell 'uses the suggestion's asset/direction' from a hardcoded SOL/long
findings.location: app/test/home_screen_test.dart:2885 (test "Trade this opens the ticket on the suggestion's asset and side"); wiring at app/lib/features/home/home_screen.dart:91-92
findings.failurePath: Only one suggestion can ever be traded in the suite (live = SOL long; the ETH short is expired at clock start), so the test checks one fixed input. Mutant: in home_screen.dart replace `symbol: item.asset,` with `symbol: 'SOL',` and `side: item.direction,` with `side: TradeSide.long,`. I ran `flutter test test/home_screen_test.dart --plain-name "maker suggestion"` on a scratch copy of app/ and got +14, all passed. No other test file references makerSuggestions, so the full suite misses it too. A feed that sent every suggestion to a SOL long ticket would ship green. The worker's M2 (side inverted to short) and the reviewer's wrong-asset ('ETH') were killed only because they changed the value away from SOL/long.
findings.fix: Add a second case on a suggestion that is not SOL long. Example: set `Scenario.clock.value = TradeMock.chartEnd.subtract(const Duration(hours: 3))` so the ETH short card is live, turn to it, tap 'Trade this', and expect `(ticket.symbol, ticket.side) == (expired.asset, expired.direction)`. The group's setUp `Scenario.reset()` restores the clock. The same test also kills the surviving clock-constant mutant (next finding).
findings.evidence: Applied the two-line mutant on an rsync copy of app/ in the session scratchpad (the worktree was not touched, and the copy was deleted afterwards). Result: all 14 tests in the 'maker suggestion' group passed. `grep -rn makerSuggestions test` matches only home_screen_test.dart. phase-5-red/mutation.log shows M2 was `short`, not a hardcoded constant.

findings.title: No test moves Scenario.clock, so the card ignoring the demo clock survives (confirms review L1)
findings.failurePath: Mutant clock-constant (`valueListenable: ValueNotifier(TradeMock.chartEnd)`) passes all 14 maker tests (mutate-run-1.txt: rc=0 SURVIVED). The same holds for a read-once variant (`Scenario.clock.value` read in build without listening), because no maker test writes Scenario.clock while a card is mounted. The only clock read in the group is `Scenario.clock.value` in the pure seeded test, which calls liveAt directly and never touches the card. The wall-clock mutant is killed, but only because chartEnd (2026-09-26 14:45) is already in the past on the wall clock. The card's link to Scenario.clock itself is unpinned.
findings.fix: In one widget test, set `Scenario.clock.value = TradeMock.chartEnd.add(const Duration(hours: 5))` with the live card on screen, pump, and expect 'Expired' with `enabled == false`. Or use the earlier-clock variant from the previous finding, which also covers it.
findings.evidence: Read the maker group: grep for Scenario.clock in home_screen_test.dart finds only line 2836. Read review-phase-5-iter-1-probe/mutate.py and mutate-run-1.txt.

findings.title: Reference-price / expiry line is never asserted (confirms review L2)
findings.failurePath: Mutant drop-reference-line deletes the 'Reference $214.90 · expires in 4h' / 'expired 2h ago' Text, and all maker tests still pass (mutate-run-2.txt SURVIVED). A wrong span sign (for example `_span(left)` on the expired branch, which prints '-2h') would also pass, as would a reference price taken from the wrong asset.
findings.fix: In the layout loop, add `expect(find.text('Reference ${s.referencePrice} · ${s == live ? 'expires in 4h' : 'expired 2h ago'}').hitTestable(), findsOneWidget)`.
findings.evidence: grep for 'Reference' and 'expires in' in home_screen_test.dart returns nothing. Read the probe's mutate-run log.

findings.title: Dead assertion: find.textContaining('Confirm') cannot fail when the ticket opens (confirms review L3)
findings.failurePath: If the expired button opened the ticket (mutant vpb-ignores-enabled), the feed ticket would show its pre-review screen. The only 'Confirm' label is built in the review panel, which appears after the ticket's action button is tapped (order_ticket.dart:956, `_ => ('Confirm', ...)`, reached only once `_review` is set). So 'Confirm' stays absent even when the sheet is open. The mutant was killed only by the BottomSheet assertion on the line above. Read on its own, the test name 'so nothing can be confirmed' overstates what this line proves.
findings.fix: Replace it with `expect(find.byType(FeedOrderTicket), findsNothing)`, or delete it. The BottomSheet check is the real guard.
findings.evidence: Read feed_order_ticket.dart (the first screen's button is the side/amount label, e.g. 'Long $200 · 2x') and order_ticket.dart:930-965. mut-vpb-ignores-enabled.log fails at 'Found 1 widget with type BottomSheet', before the Confirm line runs.

findings.title: referencePrice 'not a forked copy' check is tautological
findings.failurePath: `expect(s.referencePrice, TradeMock.quotes[s.asset]!.price)` restates the getter's own body. The comment says it guards against a forked copy, but a forked copy with today's value passes. Example: change the getter to `r'$214.90'` for SOL (and the ETH equivalent), and the test stays green until the quote changes. The test does not prove what its comment claims.
findings.fix: Either drop the comment's claim, or render-check the card text against the quote (see the reference-line finding). A rendered check catches both a missing line and a wrong source.
findings.evidence: Read maker_suggestion.dart:31 (`String get referencePrice => TradeMock.quotes[asset]!.price;`) and trade_mock.dart:95-99 (SOL price r'$214.90').

The three-dot diff lists 46 files. The app/ changes are maker_suggestion.dart (new), home_screen.dart, home_screen_test.dart and order_ticket_test.dart. The product commit is ad2176f.

Read-only state: MakerSuggestionCard reads only Scenario.clock, through a ValueListenableBuilder (maker_suggestion.dart:78-79). referencePrice reads the const TradeMock.quotes. Nothing in maker_suggestion.dart or the homeFeed itemBuilder writes to Scenario. The only `clock.value =` in lib is Scenario.reset (scenario.dart:266).

Expiry uses the demo clock: live = s.liveAt(now), where now is Scenario.clock's value and liveAt is now.isBefore(expiresAt). The fixtures are SOL at chartEnd+4h and ETH at chartEnd-2h, so at the seeded clock (TradeMock.chartEnd) SOL is live and ETH is expired. Reset puts the clock back to chartEnd and the card rebuilds through the listenable, so it stays consistent. Nothing in lib advances the clock, so a live card cannot flip while the app runs.

The expired card cannot reach the ticket. VistaPrimaryButton passes onTap: enabled ? onPressed : null (vista_flow.dart:75) and has no long-press handler. Its Semantics says enabled=false with excludeSemantics and gives no onTap, so no semantics tap action exists. The card has no other gesture detector. The onTrade closure is reachable only through that button.

Stale-closure path is not reachable: once open, the ticket is independent of the card's expiry. Only Scenario.reset writes the clock, and it writes the same chartEnd value, so the clock cannot move to cross an expiry while a ticket is open. This matches the iter-1 review's 'residual, not reachable today' note.

Prefill: home_screen.dart:89-93 passes symbol: item.asset and side: item.direction to showFeedOrderTicket. FeedOrderTicket builds OrderIntent from widget.symbol and widget.side (feed_order_ticket.dart:82-94). Scenario.placeOrder copies intent.side and intent.symbol into the receipt and the PortfolioPosition, so a fill from the SOL card opens a SOL long position.

Card copy is truthful: the badge reads 'Maker suggestion · advisory', the source reads 'Maker · demo recommendation' and the data-path line reads 'Built from Aggro demo prices'. 'Aggro' appears only in the spec/PRD, which require it as the mock data path. No text on the card claims a live source.
The reference price is the quote's display String ('$214.90' / '$2,968.40'), the same as MarketPrices._base. No new double money path: the lib diff adds no double, toDouble or division.

findings.title: Advisory badge text falls below 4.5:1 contrast (accent on accentTint)
findings.failurePath: Any device, any text scale (the 360x640 phone at 1.0x is the worst case), Home route, feed page homeFeed[2] or homeFeed[4]. The badge 'Maker suggestion · advisory' draws VistaColors.accent (#5AA6DE) text in VistaType.labelStrong (11 pt w700, so not 'large text') on VistaTag's VistaColors.accentTint (0x385AA6DE, 22% alpha) over the card's VistaColors.surface (#1F1F1F). The blended background is about rgb(44,61,73), and the contrast ratio comes out at 4.25:1, below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 for small text. This badge is the element that marks the card as advisory, and it is the hardest text on the card to read. No accent-text-on-accentTint chip exists elsewhere to set a convention: the only other accentTint use is the decorative initial circle in vista_list_row.dart:47. Accent text straight on surface would measure 6.24:1.
findings.fix: Keep the tokens but change the pairing. Either use VistaTag's defaults with an accent text colour on VistaColors.surface or surfaceRaised (accent on #1F1F1F is 6.24:1), or keep accentTint as the fill and use VistaColors.textPrimary for the label. Both choices stay token-only.
findings.evidence: Read maker_suggestion.dart:95-99, VistaTag in vista_chips.dart:35-72 (labelStrong, maxLines 1), vista_typography.dart:104 (labelStrong 11 w700) and vista_colors.dart:11/38/39. Computed the WCAG relative-luminance ratios with python3: badge 4.25, accent on surface 6.24. Ran grep for accentTint usages: only vista_list_row.dart:47 and this file.
